onboard.name: daf-onboard
onboard.description: Machine-wide DAF install: copies templates to ~/.config/agent/ and optional ~/.cursor/skills/daf-* via the onboarding script (run from DAF repo). Use when the user says /daf-onboard, global setup, or first-time machine bootstrap — before /daf-setup on a project.

setup.name: daf-setup
setup.description: Project setup after /daf-onboard: greenfield copies ~/.config/agent/scaffold into .agent/ (optional /daf-grill-me later); brownfield runs inventory + interview then merge scaffold and populate PRD/glossary/architecture; verify-state.json; optional Cursor overlay. Use when the user says /daf-setup or needs .agent/ in the project.

update.name: daf-update
update.description: Apply DAF template refresh when daf.mdc step 0 detected staleness and the user agreed, or when invoked manually: one-line daf-pin check, /daf-onboard if global-stale, daf-project-update for overlays/scaffold. Use when the user says /daf-update or accepts the session-start stale prompt.

grill-me.name: daf-grill-me
grill-me.description: Planning only: skeptical PRD interview (one question at a time, assumption audit) → PRD.md; discuss stack candidates with the user before setting config.stack. Use when the user says /daf-grill-me or wants to shape the PRD in planning phase.

realign.name: daf-realign
realign.description: Developing or maintaining: resync user intent with PRD, architecture, code, and backlog — update canon on confirmed drift. Not greenfield PRD grill (/daf-grill-me). Use when the user says /daf-realign or wants realignment while building.

start.name: daf-start
start.description: Validates planning exit, sets phase to developing when ready, and kicks off the first developing session (read backlog, one goal question). Use when the user says /daf-start or wants to begin building after planning.

help.name: daf-help
help.description: Very short DAF orientation: pillars, phases, bootstrap (/daf-onboard, /daf-setup), build loop, and which skill to use when. No code walkthrough — use /daf-how-it-works for that. Use when the user says /daf-help or wants a quick framework guide.

health.name: daf-health
health.description: One-screen status: globals, phase, verify-state, template freshness, KG presence. Runs `daf health` or packages/cli equivalent. Use when the user says /daf-health or wants a quick project health check.

how-it-works.name: daf-how-it-works
how-it-works.description: Technical implementation-precise explanation of a requested topic in this repo (flow, files, state) without code changes unless asked. Use when the user says /daf-how-it-works or wants to understand how something works in the codebase.

ltm-checkup.name: daf-ltm-checkup
ltm-checkup.description: Reconciles .agent/ canon and code with external long-term memory (e.g. Notion via MCP): drift inventory, one question at a time, confirmed doc updates only. Use when the user says /daf-ltm-checkup or wants LTM vs repo alignment.

new-feature.name: daf-new-feature
new-feature.description: Implements net-new product capability in **developing** phase (new commands, skills, flows) with acceptance checks; verification per phases/developing.md (taskCheck, verify-state, periodic codebase-check). Not for polish on existing behavior — use /daf-improvement. In **maintaining**, use only when the user explicitly opts in. Use when the user says /daf-new-feature or asks for scoped new capability while phase is developing.

issue.name: daf-issue
issue.description: Triages and fixes a reported issue in **developing** or **maintaining**: reproduce, root-cause fix (no band-aids), regression tests; verification per the current phase file. Use when the user says /daf-issue or reports a bug to fix.

improvement.name: daf-improvement
improvement.description: Improves existing code, docs, or workflow at the root (refactor, clarity, patterns) — no copy-paste workarounds; not bugs (/daf-issue) or net-new capability (/daf-new-feature). Verification per the current phase file. Use when the user says /daf-improvement or asks to make something existing better.

pivot.name: daf-pivot
pivot.description: Guides restructuring or redesign of an existing feature, concept, or architecture: from→to, blast radius, update GLOSSARY/ARCHITECTURE/PRD, migration plan, then implement per the current phase file in developing or maintaining. Not incremental polish (/daf-improvement), net-new capability (/daf-new-feature), brownfield DAF adoption (/daf-setup), or open exploration (/daf-discuss). Use when the user says /daf-pivot or decides to redesign something that already exists.

discuss.name: daf-discuss
discuss.description: Explores a topic, idea, or direction through dialogue — brainstorm and tradeoffs without implementing. Not bugs (/daf-issue), ranked build plans (/daf-improvement), PRD interviews (/daf-grill-me), or net-new builds (/daf-new-feature). Use when the user says /daf-discuss or wants to think through something before committing.

backlog-add.name: daf-backlog-add
backlog-add.description: Park a follow-up without implementing. Markdown mode: append to repo-root BACKLOG.md. Linear mode (config.integrations includes 'linear'): create a backlog issue via Linear MCP — run /daf-linear-setup first. Any phase. Use when the user says /daf-backlog-add or wants to park work for later.

backlog-work.name: daf-backlog-work
backlog-work.description: In developing or maintaining: pick an open BACKLOG.md item, classify and implement (new-feature/daf-improvement/daf-issue/daf-pivot bar), then on user acceptance remove from backlog and append a fading artifact to LOGBACK.md. When Linear is active, use /daf-linear-work instead. Use when the user says /daf-backlog-work or wants to build the next backlog item.

remember.name: daf-remember
remember.description: Saves a user-stated standing instruction to .agent/memory/remember.md for this project. Not retro takeaways (/daf-retro) or discovered gotchas. Use when the user says /daf-remember or asks the agent to always follow a project rule.

retro.name: daf-retro
retro.description: Captures short retro notes for memory/learnings or gotchas after non-trivial work. Use when the user says /daf-retro or asks for a brief retrospective.

phase-transition.name: daf-phase-transition
phase-transition.description: Validates planning exit checklist before editing config.phase to developing or maintaining (same rules as validatePlanningExit in the DAF repo). Use when the user says /daf-phase-transition or asks to leave planning.

kg-ingest.name: daf-kg-ingest
kg-ingest.description: In developing or maintaining: refresh graphify-out/ after code (npm run kg:ingest) and canonical doc changes (semantic /graphify pass). Use when the user says /daf-kg-ingest or after edits that should update the knowledge graph.

remove.name: daf-remove
remove.description: Removes DAF from the current repo: .agent/, DAF bootstrap AGENTS.md, and .cursor/rules/daf.mdc after explicit confirmation. Not machine-wide — use /daf-remove-global. Use when the user says /daf-remove or wants to strip project agent structure.

remove-global.name: daf-remove-global
remove-global.description: Uninstalls machine-wide DAF: deletes ~/.config/agent (or DAFE_GLOBAL_ROOT) and ~/.cursor/skills/daf-* folders from skill-manifest after explicit confirmation. Per-repo .agent/ remains until /daf-remove. Use when the user says /daf-remove-global or wants to uninstall /daf-onboard output.

linear-setup.name: daf-linear-setup
linear-setup.description: Enable and configure the optional Linear integration for a DAF project: lists teams and workflow states, writes linearTeam and linearTestingState to .agent/config.json, removes repo-root BACKLOG.md/LOGBACK.md, and outputs Linear + DAF best practices. Use when the user says /daf-linear-setup, wants to integrate Linear, or needs best practices for Linear-driven development.

linear-work.name: daf-linear-work
linear-work.description: Work a Linear issue inside the DAF dev loop: pick an assigned issue, set it to In Progress, implement per the current phase bar (taskCheck, verify-state, codebase-check), then move to the configured testing state and post a commit comment on acceptance. Requires config.json.integrations to include 'linear' — run /daf-linear-setup first if not configured. Use when the user says /daf-linear-work or wants to start working a Linear issue.
